title: Patient Financial Services Manual — Returned Payments Covered by a Replacement, Patient Financial Account
content:
**7.1 Clause.** Which returned payments a returned-payment replacement on the Patient Financial Account covers depends on the account's return history:

- (a) when the account has at least the tier's number of returned payments before restriction — 2 on every financial class — of returned check or ACH payments in the 12 calendar months before the handling date, every check or ACH payment returned in those 12 months is covered;
- (b) when it has exactly one in those 12 months and at least one more in the 24 calendar months before the handling date, every check or ACH payment returned in those 24 months is covered;
- (c) otherwise, no wider coverage applies under this clause.

The covered returned amount is the total of the amounts returned by the payments covered.

**7.2 Counting returns.** A returned check or ACH payment is a payment reversal on the account ledger whose method was check or ACH, counted by the date of the reversal; a card chargeback is not counted. A window of calendar months for the returned-payment replacement ends on the handling date and reaches back that many months, a date on the same calendar day that many months earlier falling outside it.

## Judgement table

| Returns in the 12 months | Returns in the 24 months | Covered |
|---|---|---|
| 2 or more | any | every check or ACH return in the 12 months |
| exactly 1 | 2 or more | every check or ACH return in the 24 months |
| exactly 1 | 1 | no wider coverage under this clause |
| 0 | any | no wider coverage under this clause |

## Worked cases (hypothetical, handling date 10 October 2026)

- Returns of 120.00 on 2 February 2026 and 90.00 on 1 September 2026: two in 12 months, so both are covered, 210.00.
- A return of 90.00 on 1 September 2026 and one of 60.00 on 15 March 2025: one in 12 months and two in 24 months, so both are covered, 150.00.
- A return of 90.00 on 1 September 2026 and one of 60.00 on 10 October 2024: the older one falls on the same calendar day 24 months earlier, outside the 24 months, so (b) does not apply.
